caption: Table 1. Agreement between DUET and R MAST 1.33.0 on identical cells, genes and model (~1 + condition). Genes: genes tested by both implementations. Jaccard: significant-gene sets at BH-adjusted p < 0.05. The simulation row gives the median over 100 muscat replicates. Pancreas values use the corrected object.

Table 2. Matched benchmark on pancreas data: median of five runs per engine after one warm-up, single-threaded, identical input file. CPU ratio: MAST/DUET end-to-end CPU time. Fit + test ratio: MAST zlm + lrTest against DUET's fit-and-test stage, elapsed time. Peak: resident memory of the process tree. The machine was in use during the benchmark (median background CPU load 9–31%).

Table 3. Performance against muscat ground truth over 100 independent replicates (4,000 genes, 24,000 cells, four versus four samples). Sensitivity and observed FDR at a nominal BH level of 0.05, mean ± SD. Calibrated threshold: the score threshold giving a mean observed FDR of 5% on replicates 1–50, evaluated on replicates 51–100. The two-stage rule has the ROC-AUC of DUET's ranking and the calls of the pseudobulk arm.

Table 4. Percentage of genes called significant (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) by simulated category, mean ± SD over 100 replicates. High values are desirable for the four alternative categories and low values for the two null categories; in the null categories every call is a false discovery.

Table 6. Donor-swap global null over all unique balanced donor partitions: percentage of genes rejected (BH-adjusted p < 0.05), mean ± SD over partitions. Every rejection is a false positive; the values are rejection proportions, not false discovery rates. DESeq2 and the two-stage rule agree at displayed precision, but differ in two partitions; separate exact summaries and discovery frequencies are supplied in Table S16. The same partitions are shown in Fig. 4d. Pancreas rows are technical sensitivity analyses.

Table 5. Calibration on the genes muscat labels as nulls (ee and ep), averaged over 100 replicates (range across replicates in brackets). The BH denominators are within 1% of one another, so the differences between rows are in the p-values and not in the multiple-testing correction. Quartiles are of the per-gene design effect 1 + (m̄ − 1)·ICC with m̄ = 3,000 cells per sample. Valid conservative tests may have super-uniform rather than uniform p-values; null-gene rejection proportions are not FDR.

Table 7. Donor-aware cell-level models against DUET and its two-stage rule on simulation replicates 51–70, subsampled to 500 cells per sample (all methods on the same cells). Separate rows reflect different scored-gene universes (GLIMES: 2,211–3,330; MAST: 3,927–3,994), not verified different cell subsamples. Compare methods within each stratum. Donor-swap null results: Additional file 2, Table S13.
